correctness.rationale: Every graph is fully specified by a labeled cubic edge list. A direct edge-subset enumerator and a logically independent cut-partition-and-completion enumerator both exhaust their finite state spaces, yield no edge-cut-dominating set at one below each claimed minimum, and return exactly identical minimum sets after edge-order normalization. Upward closure excludes smaller values. The endpoint-union criterion is equivalent to edge domination; residual connectivity includes isolated vertices. The certified complete lists contain 98, 8, 27, 5 masks; their component shapes and crossing-edge counts are all checked. Vertex-permutation witnesses are individually tested as genuine automorphisms mapping representatives to all listed minima. The edge-domination numbers use a cubic five-edge coverage lower bound and exhaustive existence/nonexistence at the critical sizes. Reproduction: edgecut.cpp, edgecut_partition.cpp, certificate.json, verify_certificate.py, both complete recorded outputs and verification.out. There is no claim outside these four finite graphs.

originality.rationale: The exact four-graph joint theorem (98, 8, 27, 5 minimum edge-cut dominating sets; all component profiles and six automorphism orbits; constrained-vs-unconstrained gaps) is neither stated nor implied by the two materially inspected primary papers. The 2016 introduction gives general definitions/bounds and values for complete graphs, cycles, wheels, complete bipartite graphs, paths and trees; the 2022 incidence-graph work studies ordinary edge domination and incidence-free sets without imposing an edge-disconnecting deletion. Distinct published three-cut-complex homotopy and L1 cut-cone findings concern other invariants and do not recover selected-edge endpoint-cover constraints. Multiple published-record and indexed scientific-record searches found no direct covering record. This is a best-evidence self-review, not proof of priority; the 2004 original split-edge paper full text was inaccessible.

value.rationale: This precisely answers the natural comparison raised by the edge-cut-domination literature: what additional edge cost is required to disrupt connectivity while maintaining edge domination? Four canonical cubic bipartite symmetric graphs realize both equality and a one-edge price (1,0,1,0) and admit an unexpectedly rigid exact classification: 98 Heawood optima in three geometrically different automorphism orbits versus single balanced-cut orbits of sizes 8, 27 and 5 in the other three. The claim resolves full natural minimum-set families, not arbitrary sampled subfamilies; its cut geometries provide concrete extremal benchmarks and structural counterpoint for cut-dominating graph theory. No speculative general theorem or exaggerated impact is asserted.
